Added a new variant section. The reference now covers the z-score statistic and the maturity-schedule table source with the end-of-February multi-bulletin reading pattern.

Memory is at 99% capacity, so I won't add a new memory entry — the skill reference captures this fully, and the question went CORRECT anyway (no recurring failure to flag). The skill is the right home for this procedural knowledge.

Summary of what I saved (to descriptive-stats-over-months.md):
- New "Z-SCORE over a multi-YEAR series" variant: z = (value − mean)/std(ddof=1), both stats from the same N-year sample, keep the sign (below-mean → negative), round only at the end.
- The maturity-schedule table as a data source (interest-bearing marketable public debt by maturity year), and the "outstanding at end of February for each year" = read N different Bulletin issues (one end-Feb snapshot per year), a multi-bulletin stitch — not all values from one issue's forward schedule.
- Diagnostics: ~12% magnitude miss (N=5) = wrong ddof; right magnitude/wrong sign = reported |z|.

This was a clean CORRECT run, but the z-score convention and the maturity-schedule source were both genuinely new and reusable, so saving was warranted.
